cases.title: Expressive public workshop landing page
cases.starter_shortcomings: Legible functional baseline with weak typographic hierarchy, undifferentiated sections, generic composition, and limited connection between the printmaking subject and layout. Do not reward a particular font or style recipe.

design: Art direction feels specific to a small hands-on print studio and welcoming to beginners.
Hierarchy communicates the offer and routes visitors toward choosing a workshop.
Composition, typography, spacing, imagery, and details form an intentional whole across both widths.
Workshop comparison and practical information remain easy to find.
technical: Workshop choices populate the reservation control correctly; valid input produces an honest local preview.
Navigation, form controls, focus, labels, and messages remain usable with keyboard and assistive technology.
Page content reflows at 390px and 320px without clipped text or body overflow.
Supplied facts and assets remain represented accurately; no remote asset dependency is introduced.
workflow: Makes a defensible direction choice and completes work without unnecessary preference checkpoints.
Inspects rendered output and distinguishes aesthetic critique from interaction verification.
Reports actual checks and unresolved limitations without unsupported claims.
hard_failures: Reservation or workshop-selection flow no longer works.
Changes prices, dates, venue, cancellation policy, or claims a real booking was sent.
Introduces an unauthorized framework, external booking service, or fabricated endorsement.
Primary content or action is inaccessible at narrow widths or by keyboard.

scenarios.actions: Choose monoprinting, then block printing from the workshop sections.
scenarios.expected: Each action reaches the reservation form with the corresponding workshop selected.

scenarios.actions: Submit with required fields empty, then submit Ada with ada@example.test and block printing.
scenarios.expected: Missing inputs are identified; valid submission produces a preview for October 8 at $68 CAD and clearly states no real booking/payment occurred.

scenarios.actions: Navigate links and complete the form using only keyboard; inspect 390px and 320px widths and 200% zoom.
scenarios.expected: Visible focus, operable controls, coherent reading order, useful tap targets, no lost content or body overflow.

cases.title: Dense existing Vue operational interface
cases.starter_shortcomings: Working search/filter/sort/detail behavior. Large metric cards waste space, status styling lacks useful prioritization, repeated View controls lack job context, and the fixed sidebar/table cause narrow-screen page overflow. Detail selection has no focus management. Keep table-level scrolling acceptable when surrounding controls remain reachable and the region is usable.

design: Retains recognizable teal/slate Harbor identity and a compact operational composition.
At-risk jobs, due times, and handoff information are easy to find without relying on color alone.
Balances useful table density with readable alignment, grouping, and control hierarchy.
Responsive layout preserves important work rather than hiding information to make a screenshot fit.
technical: Search by ID/customer/destination combines correctly with the status filter; empty results are understandable and recoverable.
Due-time sorting reverses the order without losing or mutating source jobs.
Details show the selected job and note; opening and closing remain usable by keyboard.
All 12 jobs, 3 at-risk jobs, 5 ready jobs, brand tokens, and Vue Composition API/TypeScript remain intact.
Build succeeds; no uncaught browser errors; controls and content work at wide and narrow widths.
workflow: Works within the established design system and task scope.
Verifies real search/filter/sort/detail behavior as well as rendered hierarchy.
Avoids new backend, dependencies, unrelated charts, or fictional operational metrics.
hard_failures: Removes or breaks search, filtering, sorting, or accurate job details.
Discards the supplied dataset, stack, or Harbor identity.
Introduces an inaccessible essential control or loses critical information at mobile width.
Build fails or the page produces an uncaught runtime error.

scenarios.actions: Choose At risk; search Little Atlas. Then clear search, search Riverside with All statuses, and search a nonexistent customer.
scenarios.expected: Little Atlas returns only HB-1046; At risk alone returns HB-1042/HB-1046/HB-1051; Riverside returns HB-1044/HB-1049; unmatched text shows an understandable empty state.

scenarios.actions: With all filters clear, toggle due-time sorting twice.
scenarios.expected: Ascending begins HB-1042 at 14:00 and ends HB-1053 at 16:00; descending reverses those endpoints. All 12 jobs remain available.

scenarios.actions: Open HB-1046 details and close them; repeat using only the keyboard.
scenarios.expected: Little Atlas, J. Okafor, 4 parcels, 14:30, At risk, and the missing-label note appear accurately. Focus stays visible and returns to a useful place after closing.

scenarios.actions: Inspect at 1440px, 390px, and 320px; operate search/filter and inspect a selected job.
scenarios.expected: Controls remain visible and operable, text remains readable, and any horizontal scrolling is contained to a usable data region rather than the entire page.

cases.title: Accessible appointment request flow
cases.starter_shortcomings: Inputs have visual text but no programmatic labels; focus outlines removed; fixed grid overflows; validation checks only truthiness and has one generic message; email format unchecked; whitespace accepted; async status not announced; duplicate submissions allowed; confirmation cannot be revised. Candidate is allowed to fix these defects as part of the explicit brief.

design: Calm readable hierarchy explains what the request means and makes progress through the form clear.
Validation, loading, failure, and confirmation states receive appropriate emphasis without destabilizing the page.
Helpful context supports the form and remains usable at narrow widths.
technical: Every field has a programmatic name, required/optional expectations, visible focus, and useful input/autocomplete semantics.
Missing/whitespace-only required values and malformed email are rejected; errors identify affected fields and are accessible.
Submission progress is exposed and duplicate requests are prevented while pending.
Service errors preserve all entered values and permit retry without re-entering information.
Success communicates request details and reference; revise returns to the populated editable form with useful focus.
Reflow, zoom, contrast, keyboard order, target sizes, and any added motion support accessibility.
workflow: Exercises actual failure/retry/success states using supplied deterministic API behavior.
Keeps validation/interface changes proportionate and does not modify the API to bypass errors.
Separates observed checks from unperformed screen-reader or conformance audits.
hard_failures: Changes api.js behavior or sends data to an external service.
Submission loses entered data on failure or creates duplicate requests while pending.
Required controls or error recovery are unavailable by keyboard.
No working success or revise path, or confirmation falsely claims an actual appointment is booked.

scenarios.actions: Submit an empty form; then try whitespace name/purpose and a malformed email.
scenarios.expected: No API request occurs. Errors identify affected controls and focus/announcements make recovery understandable.

scenarios.actions: Fill Alex Reed, retry@example.test, October 13, family research, a note requesting an adjustable desk, and agreement. Submit twice rapidly, wait for failure, then retry.
scenarios.expected: Only one call starts while pending; all values survive the first failure; second intentional request succeeds with NB-2046.

scenarios.actions: Reload and submit valid values with unavailable@example.test twice.
scenarios.expected: Each request fails accessibly; data remains intact, retry remains available, and no success is fabricated.

scenarios.actions: Complete a successful request, then choose the revise/edit action.
scenarios.expected: Confirmation includes accurate details and local-demo meaning; form returns with previous values and logical keyboard focus.

scenarios.actions: Complete the form with keyboard only and inspect 390px/320px, 200% zoom, and reduced-motion preference.
scenarios.expected: Labels and errors remain associated; focus is visible; no body overflow or clipped content; added animation respects reduced motion.

cases.title: Content-heavy public walking guide
cases.starter_shortcomings: Generic title, missing description and lang, accidental noindex, div-based headings/landmarks, pointer-only contents links, missing image alternative and table headers, wide prose measure, and fixed-width map overflow. All substantive copy exists in the initial HTML; no external fetch is needed.

design: Reading hierarchy and typographic measure make the long guide comfortable and scannable.
Route facts, access limitations, and seasonal caution are easy to locate without flattening the whole page into equal cards.
Visual identity suits a modest local walking guide, and the route map supports the content.
Desktop and mobile navigation serve long-form reading without obscuring content.
technical: Landmarks, ordered heading levels, real fragment links, image alternative, and table headers convey content structure.
The main title, summary, body, route facts, and links remain available in initial HTML.
Production-appropriate title/description/canonical and indexing intent match the specified public URL; no conflicting noindex remains.
Contents links work by keyboard and preserve usable fragment navigation; anchors are not obscured by sticky elements.
Map, table, prose, and long content reflow without page overflow or hidden facts at narrow widths.
workflow: Preserves factual route limitations and distinguishes illustrative fixture content from live travel advice.
Checks rendered reading quality and public-page semantics/indexing separately.
Adds no unsupported live maps, tracking, framework, or unnecessary structured-data claims.
hard_failures: Omits or reverses the full-loop step/access limitations or floodwater caution.
Changes route distances, timing, publication date, or transport facts without authorization.
Leaves the production-intended page marked noindex or makes essential content dependent on external fetch.
Main navigation or essential route information is inaccessible by keyboard or at mobile width.

scenarios.actions: Use keyboard to follow every contents link, then load /#access directly and use Back to top.
scenarios.expected: Real fragments address the correct sections, headings remain visible, and navigation works with scripts disabled.

scenarios.actions: Find the full loop distance, step-free option, Orchard Lane steps, toilet hours, and rain advice.
scenarios.expected: 5.2 km/1 hour 45 minutes; 2.4 km return step-free outing; 12 steps; 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; do not enter floodwater or pass closure signs.

scenarios.actions: Inspect initial HTML and response metadata locally.
scenarios.expected: Meaningful title/description, en language, canonical https://walks.alderwick.example/guides/river-loop/, indexable intent, crawlable fragment links, and substantive content without JavaScript.

scenarios.actions: Inspect top/middle/bottom at 1440px and 390px, plus 320px and 200% zoom.
scenarios.expected: Readable line lengths, useful heading hierarchy, accessible map/table, no clipped or hidden route details, and no horizontal body scrolling.
